ModMetaData.name: RimMCP
ModMetaData.author: rakan
ModMetaData.description:
Agentic intelligence - Now brought to the Rim.
RimMCP connects your colony to any AI agent that speaks MCP. Your agent will be able to see and do almost anything in the game: lay out zones, build, order pawns, run time forward, and tell you anything about the game.
For the modern high-impact 10x engineer looking to utilize agentic AI to drive business value in their colony.
What can it do? • See what you see. Pawns, stockpiles, bills, research, threats, the map itself, even your mod list and error log. • Tell you what's wrong. Why nobody is cooking, why the field isn't sown, what's about to rot. • Run the colony. Zones, stockpiles, blueprints, mining, bills, work priorities, policies, research. • Command your pawns. Draft, move, attack, rescue, tend, equip. • Mind the clock. Let time run, and pause the moment something goes wrong.
Fair play • Plays by the rules. Everything goes through the game's own right-click menus, designators and placement rules. The Agent can't cheat. • No peeking. Fog of war applies. It can't see information not available to you. • Access control. Choose how much access the agent has under Access in mod settings: Full control (default): do everything, including storyteller and difficulty. Control: do everything except change game settings. Administration: read, manage colony settings and run time, but not give direct orders. Read only: look, but no actions.
Requirements • RimWorld 1.6 or 1.7. • An AI client with support for local (stdio) MCP servers. Tested with Codex & OpenCode.
Setup 1. Enable RimMCP in your mod list and restart the game. 2. Go to Options > Mod settings > RimMCP and click Copy MCP config. 3. Add that config to your client's MCP settings (or paste it to your agent and tell it to configure itself, who has time to edit tomls nowadays). 4. Turn on RimWorld's Run in background option so requests work while you're alt-tabbed.
Frequently asked Mid-save compatible? Yes. RimMCP does not save anything on your colony. Feel free to add or remove at will. Performance? Near 0 impact when idling. When your agent calls tools, most requests are handled in milliseconds. Multiplayer? Your agent can look, but anything that changes the game or the clock is refused during a Multiplayer session. Privacy? If your client uses a cloud model, it may send colony data to that provider. Your colony data could help shape the mind of future LLMs, what could possibly go wrong?
Source: https://github.com/rakanssh/rimcp | Bugs: https://github.com/rakanssh/rimcp/issues
